DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION Livinopril monotherapy is an effective treatment of hypertension in once-daily doses of 10 mg to 50 mg, while hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy is effective in doses of 12.5 mg to 50 mg per day. In clinical trials of lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide combination therapy using lisinopril doses of 10 mg to 80 mg and hydrochlorothiaride doses of 6.25 mg to 50 mg. the untihypertensive response rates generally increased with increasing dose of either component. The side effects (sce WARNINGS ) of lisinopril are generally rare and apparently independent of dose; those of hydrochlorothiazide are a mixture of dose-dependent phenomena (primarily hypokalemia) and dose-independent phenomena (c.g-- pancreatitis), the former much more common than the latter. Therapy with any combination of lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide will he associated with both sets of dose-independent side effects, but addition of lisinopril in clinical trials blunted the hypokalemia normally seen with diuretics. To minimize dose-independent side effects, it is usually appropriate to begin combination therapy only after a patient has failed touchieve the desired effect with monotherapy. Dose Titration Guided by Clinical Effect A patient whose blood pressure is not adequately controlled with either lisinopril or hydrochlorothiazide monotherapy may be switched to lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide tablets 10 mg/12,5 mg or lisinopril und hydrochlorothiazide tablets 20 mg/12.5 mg. Further increases of cither or both components could depend on clinical response. The hydrochlorothiazide dose should generally not be increased until 2-3 weeks have clapsed.
